preamble: Secondary palatalization of the voiced velar stop [ɡ] to [ɡʲ] before front vowels or a palatal glide. In Russian, velars became allophonically palatalized before /i/ between the 12th and 14th centuries, which turned the old sequence gy into gʲi (Old Russian гыбкыи [ɡɨpkɨj] > гибкий [ɡʲipkʲij] 'flexible'). In Japanese, consonants are palatalized before /i/ and /j/ (ぎょうざ gyōza with [ɡʲ]).

examples.note: Velars became palatalized before /i/ (from earlier /ɨ/ after velars) between the 12th and 14th centuries; spelling ги- replaced гы-.

examples.from: /ɡj/ in ぎょうざ gyōza 'fried dumpling'
examples.note: Only palatalized consonants occur before /i/; they are often analysed as allophones conditioned by a following /i/ or /j/.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). History of the Russian language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Russian_language
